competitor: Epic MyChart (patient portal; proxy / family access)

works_well.theme: See a loved one's test results and doctor notes
works_well.what_it_means: Caregivers read results, notes and diagnoses for the person they care for, often before or instead of a phone call.

quotes.quote: I have access to her “my chart” and can see doctor’s notes.
By accessing their MyChart accounts, we can debunk their story by reading the report and we know in great detail what the doctor said and what was recommended.

works_well.theme: Several family members' records under one login
works_well.what_it_means: Caregivers like seeing their own chart plus a parent's, spouse's or children's charts without switching accounts.

quotes.quote: now I can include and manage my mother’s account without switching
Allows me to see both my husband's and my records with a single log in.

works_well.theme: Message a loved one's doctor directly
works_well.what_it_means: Caregivers send questions and updates to the patient's care team through the app and often get quick replies.

quotes.quote: it allows me to communicate with my mom's doctor and he always replies the same day.
I sent the ingredients list to her doctor through MyChart who replied with a very clear "NO."

works_well.theme: Track a loved one's appointments and medicines
works_well.what_it_means: Caregivers use it to keep up with another person's visits, medicine lists and treatment plans.

quotes.quote: this app has been of paramount importance in tracking my wife's many appointments battling cancer.
proxy access helps me with managing appointments for dependents' too.

works_well.theme: Keep up from far away without waiting on phone calls
works_well.what_it_means: Long-distance caregivers follow a parent's care from another state or country.

quotes.quote: this mychart keeps me up to date on everything and helps my stress levels so much no waiting for a fon call or sitting on hold for 30 mins
It helped me a lot follow up on my mom's medical condition from outside the country.

works_well.theme: Follow a hospital stay day by day
works_well.what_it_means: Family members watch treatment, medicines and vitals while a loved one is in the hospital.

quotes.quote: this app allowed me to see the actual treatment to my husband while he was hospitalized.
When a loved one is hospitalized, daily care notes are informative and comforting.

works_well.theme: Records ready to hand to others
works_well.what_it_means: Caregivers pull up or download a loved one's records for schools, new facilities, doctors or siblings.

quotes.quote: capture screenshots and save files to share with my brothers and other caregivers
downloaded some key records from MyChart/Epic and created a CareEverywhere link for the rest.

works_well.theme: Less stress and more comfort for the caregiver
works_well.what_it_means: Seeing what is happening calms the caregiver.

quotes.quote: It gave me comfort to know day to day his treatment, and his medications.
helps my stress levels so much

does_not_work_well.theme: Older loved ones can't or won't use it themselves
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: The patient has no phone, poor memory, poor sight or hearing, or refuses to go online, so the work falls on family.

quotes.quote: THE THING SHE DOESN'T HAVE AND WOULDN'T UNDERSTAND HOW TO USE???
cannot create account for my husband. he doesn't have a mobile phone.

does_not_work_well.theme: No caregiver login of their own, so families share the patient's password
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Caregivers log in as the patient, which causes code hassles, lockouts and family fights over who holds the password.

quotes.quote: They should make it so that when they have caregivers, we should have our own logons.
Arguing over the right to a password for MyChart as some sort of weird power move.

does_not_work_well.theme: Getting access to a loved one's chart is hard to set up
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Sign-up codes go to the patient's phone, the patient must be present, or a spouse can't be added.

quotes.quote: I asked for the sign-up code and they insisted on sending it to her.
I could t sign up for it without having her present to talk to the admin

does_not_work_well.theme: The patient's privacy wishes clash with family access
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Parents block or resent family access, or caregivers worry the patient will see what they write to doctors.

quotes.quote: there was a note that patient had called that morning requesting that the office no longer communicate with any of her 3 daughters.
will my mom be able to see the message and the doctor's reply from her myChart?

does_not_work_well.theme: Logging into a spouse's account keeps failing
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Lockouts, password resets and updates stop people from getting into a husband's or wife's account.

quotes.quote: can not sign into my wife's account after update. can sign into mine.
She has to change the password everytime.

does_not_work_well.theme: Parents lose or struggle to get access to a minor child's chart
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Parents of children and young teens find access hard to start or cut off before age 18.

quotes.quote: I, as a mom, should be allowed access to my child's medical records and not be told to go to the office and create a "teen account".
I also don't understand why parents lose or have limited access to their child's records before they turn 18.

does_not_work_well.theme: Managing several family members in one app is clumsy
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: With more than one patient, notices don't say who they are about and adding people is hard.

quotes.quote: Getting a random notification that " you have a new test result" but not knowing which family member ( when 3 were at the doctor yesterday) stinks!!!
I need to add a third patient. It’s not really user friendly app.

does_not_work_well.theme: Clinics send important news only through the app
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Surgery dates, closures, bills and pharmacy questions arrive as MyChart messages instead of a call, and get missed.

quotes.quote: "Well we sent a message out in MyChart." Are you fucking serious? She doesn't even have MyChart set up!
I got a message in my mom’s MyChart that they’d scheduled the surgery a week from today.

does_not_work_well.theme: Results show up before anyone explains them
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Raw results and notes cause worry or confusion until a doctor talks to the family.

quotes.quote: they get posted to MyChart sometimes before the doctor comes in, and this parent will fret over minor things
She calls me and blithely announces "MyChart says I've got chlamydia!"

does_not_work_well.theme: Messages and refill requests go unanswered
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Caregivers' MyChart messages and requests are not answered or not passed on without extra calls.

quotes.quote: She also doesn’t respond to my chart messages.
it takes multiple voicemails and my chart messages to kick off the process.

does_not_work_well.theme: Sharing records outside MyChart is hard
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: Blocked screenshots, outside care teams that can't open links, and huge exports make sharing hard.

quotes.quote: When i need to share data with family and caregiver consultant, I can't !!!!
hampered by the deluge of PDF, CSV, HTML, and RTF files to sort through.

does_not_work_well.theme: Slow or missing updates during a long hospital stay
does_not_work_well.what_it_means: During a family member's hospital stay, results lag or pile up with no easy way to sort them.

quotes.quote: Takes too long to refresh , which makes it hard to keep up to date with  my family member’s hospitalization.
I liked this app UNTIL it became important with a family member's hospitalization.

who_uses_and_who_pays.theme: Adult children and grandchildren managing a parent's care
who_uses_and_who_pays.what_it_means: The largest group: grown children (and some grandchildren, nieces, in-laws) following an aging relative's care, often from far away.

quotes.quote: I do all my mom's online stuff for her. I pay all her medical bills. I email her doctors for her. I make her appointments.
for aging parents, you can get onto their information as a proxy to help manage their appointments and etc.

who_uses_and_who_pays.what_it_means: Husbands and wives track or log into each other's accounts.

quotes.quote: I can keep up with my Drs appts and my husband's appts and everything about us

who_uses_and_who_pays.theme: Parents managing a minor child's chart
who_uses_and_who_pays.what_it_means: Parents of children and teens; kept separate from care of adults.

quotes.quote: It’s so convenient and easy to use to view my charts and my kids charts.
is a really helpful tool for parents, I keep in touch whit my kids doctors tru de app

who_uses_and_who_pays.theme: Caregivers pay the loved one's medical bills through it

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: Getting access to a loved one's chart is hard to set up
relatives_joining_and_sharing.what_it_means: Codes, in-person visits and phone requirements slow down adding a relative.

quotes.quote: Difficult for the parent to get the app started for a minor.

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: No caregiver login of their own, so families share the patient's password

quotes.quote: she had given me her login credentials to help her schedule and keep up with appts, etc

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: Proxy access lets one person see another's chart from their own login

quotes.quote: I have proxy access for my mom, so, from my own MyChart, I can get her test results, read appointment notes, and send messages to her doctors.
proxy access helps me with managing appointments for dependents' too.

relatives_joining_and_sharing.theme: Siblings and other helpers get updates by screenshots or files
relatives_joining_and_sharing.what_it_means: There is no shared view for a wider family group, so the main caregiver passes things on by hand.

quotes.quote: capture screenshots and save files to share with my brothers and other caregivers

emergencies_and_support_response.theme: In urgent moments, app messages did not replace a phone call

quotes.quote: outrageously complex and difficult to add my minor to my account.

setup_and_ease_of_use.what_it_means: Caregivers who have access call it user friendly.

privacy_data_trust.theme: The patient's privacy wishes clash with family access
privacy_data_trust.what_it_means: Patients block family, resent lookups, or caregivers want private notes to the doctor.

quotes.quote: she says it's because I look things up on MyChart and ask "wrong" questions

single_mentions.point: After a loved one died, the caregiver could no longer log in and asked whether the account is deleted forever.
A father's VA home care team could not open outside links on government phones, so they could not see his hospital progress.
A nurse's notes, including a report to Adult Protective Services, were accidentally posted to the mother's MyChart where the daughter read them.
A retired nurse uses it to help friends and family, not just herself.
A paid caregiver handles her client's medical tasks on the client's MyChart.
Caregiver printed an AI-made medicine calendar to hang on the fridge alongside MyChart notes.

reader_notes: Kept 78 of 279: 9 of 200 Apple reviews, all 33 Google reviews, 36 of 46 Reddit posts. The 200 Apple reviews were not caregiving-filtered and are almost all patients writing about their own care (191 dropped as not caregiving); 4 Reddit posts were also dropped as the writer's own care. Who the caregiver is caring for, across the 78 kept: adult children / grandchildren / nieces / in-laws caring for an older relative = 42 (1 Apple, 8 Google, 33 Reddit); spouses = 15 (14 Google, 1 Reddit); parents of a minor child = 9 (4 Apple: c-90, c-100, c-152, c-191; 5 Google: gp-mychart-1, -4, -11, -41, -55), counted separately as asked; paid caregiver = 1 (reddit-p1tjv80m); unclear or mixed relation = 11. Minor-child items split: 5 praise seeing kids' records in one place, 4 complain that access for a parent is hard to start or is cut off before 18 (c-152, gp-mychart-1, -11, -55). Google reviews are short (often one sentence) and date Jul-Nov 2026; Apple reviews are all Oct 26-Nov 1 2026, one week only; Reddit posts span Jan 2023-Oct 2026, mostly r/CaregiverSupport and r/AgingParents, and carry the detail on proxy access and shared passwords. Several Reddit posts mention MyChart in passing inside longer stories; they were kept when they say how it was used. Two Reddit posts were cut at 4000 characters in the pack and had no MyChart mention in the kept text, so they were dropped. reddit-p1hyanlq is the same post as reddit-p1hyaqd5 in another subreddit; only one is counted. No item mentions a price for MyChart itself, so cost_price_cancelling is empty; the money talk is about paying the loved one's medical bills. gp-mychart-56 is written by the patient who wants to share with family and caregivers (kept because it passed the caregiving filter and is about family sharing). MyChart is run by each hospital or clinic, so features such as proxy access, teen-account rules and two-step login differ by organization; reviews cannot tell which rules are Epic's and which are the clinic's.
